headline: HSC pass rate drops to 52.12%, falling by 6.71 percentage points
summary: Nearly 600,000 students failed this year's HSC and equivalent exams, with 293 institutions recording a zero pass rate.
details: The overall pass rate for this year’s Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations has fallen to 52.12 percent, a drop of 6.71 percentage points from last year’s 58.83 percent.
Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon announced the results on Saturday, following exams that began on July 2 across 2,697 centres nationwide.
Out of 1,240,798 candidates who took part in the exams, 40,084 students secured a GPA-5.
The decline in pass rates was observed across all nine general education boards, as well as the Madrasa and Technical boards.
A striking detail reveals that 293 educational institutions recorded a zero pass rate, meaning no student from those schools passed the exams.
The number of GPA-5 achievers has dropped by more than half in the last two years.
caption:
Nearly 600,000 students failed their HSC exams this year as the pass rate plummeted to 52.12%.

The overall pass rate for this year’s Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations has fallen to 52.12 percent, a drop of 6.71 percentage points from last year’s 58.83 percent.

Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon announced the results on Saturday, following exams that began on July 2 across 2,697 centres nationwide.

Out of 1,240,798 candidates who took part in the exams, 40,084 students secured a GPA-5.

The decline in pass rates was observed across all nine general education boards, as well as the Madrasa and Technical boards.

A striking detail reveals that 293 educational institutions recorded a zero pass rate, meaning no student from those schools passed the exams.

The number of GPA-5 achievers has dropped by more than half in the last two years.

headline: Father of former Air Force officer Tahsif Sawri files murder case
summary: The case was lodged three days after Tahsif's body was recovered from the Turag River, leading to the detention of a close acquaintance.
details: KM Enayetul Karim, the father of former Air Force officer Tahsif Sawri, has filed a murder case with Uttarkhan police against unidentified persons.
The case was registered on Friday night, three days after Tahsif's body was found floating in the Rajabari Ghat area of the Turag River on Wednesday.
Following the filing of the case, Ahmed Shahriar Reza Dwip, a younger acquaintance of Tahsif, was placed in detention.
Dwip had been detained for questioning by the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) since Thursday night after being identified as the last person with Tahsif.
According to PBI, Dwip confessed that they were in a drug hotspot area in Tongi on Tuesday night when a police team chased them, causing Tahsif to jump into the river.
Tahsif's motorcycle was recovered from the Mazar slum area of Tongi on Friday morning based on information provided by Dwip.
The River Police are now leading the probe into the circumstances of the death.
Tahsif had previously gained attention for allegedly sharing a video of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina's departure from Bangladesh.
caption:
A former Air Force officer's body was found in the Turag River. Now, his father has finally filed a murder case.

KM Enayetul Karim, the father of former Air Force officer Tahsif Sawri, has filed a murder case with Uttarkhan police against unidentified persons.

The case was registered on Friday night, three days after Tahsif's body was found floating in the Rajabari Ghat area of the Turag River on Wednesday.

Following the filing of the case, Ahmed Shahriar Reza Dwip, a younger acquaintance of Tahsif, was placed in detention.

Dwip had been detained for questioning by the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) since Thursday night after being identified as the last person with Tahsif.

According to PBI, Dwip confessed that they were in a drug hotspot area in Tongi on Tuesday night when a police team chased them, causing Tahsif to jump into the river.

Tahsif's motorcycle was recovered from the Mazar slum area of Tongi on Friday morning based on information provided by Dwip.

The River Police are now leading the probe into the circumstances of the death.

Tahsif had previously gained attention for allegedly sharing a video of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina's departure from Bangladesh.
